title: Due process hearings
question: When is a hearing due, and what kind?

steps.note: An individualized assessment requires a hearing.
A general rule affecting many needs no individual hearing.
Welfare recipients get a pre-termination evidentiary hearing.
Property interests come from an entitlement, not from the Constitution; no interest for a one-year professor.
De facto tenure can be a property interest.
The “bitter with the sweet” plurality; later rejected.
Three-factor balancing: private interest, risk of error, government burden.
Some pre-termination process for tenured public employees; the bitter-with-the-sweet idea is dead.
